recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for this issue unless a future work group decision redefines DocumentReference.date or its relationship to Attachment.creation.
issue_request: FHIR-43625 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core DocumentReference. It requested changing DocumentReference.date from instant to dateTime because only a calendar date is often known for historical documents, and adding guidance to use the most precise timestamp available.
initial_application: The change was already applied before this reconciliation. Commit d63adb6a17972d47bde74e7377febe531b104a9a changed source/documentreference/structuredefinition-DocumentReference.xml from instant to dateTime and added the requested precision comment; it also removed the Event.recorded mapping-exception type mismatch for DocumentReference.date.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists documentreference=DocumentReference, confirming the inspected DocumentReference source is in current build scope. The DocumentReference date search parameter remains type=date, which is the correct FHIR search parameter type and not a contradiction of the element datatype. Related FHIR-43927 and FHIR-25205 distinguish DocumentReference.date from content attachment creation timing and do not reverse this datatype change. OO WGM minutes on 2024-05-20 record the motion to accept the datatype change 8-0-0; focused Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed because the combined branch already has DocumentReference.date as dateTime and includes the requested 'Provide the most precise timestamp available' guidance.

related_jiras.note: Resolved - No Change request to broaden or supplement DocumentReference.date; confirms content-specific creation dates are handled by Attachment.creation and the creation search parameter.
